text:
alex_infra: Heads up — ap-south-1 training fleet seeing big allreduce slowdowns after last night's infra rollout. 50-70% bandwidth drop on NCCL, jobs falling back to TCP. Anyone see related RDMA/QP errors?

sam_ml: Yep noticed it on a few runs this morning, logs show NCCL falling back and *much* higher latency. Wondering if it's the kernel bump + new nvidia driver combo.

jenna_oncall: Deploy bot flagged the OFED package update at 02:12 UTC. I rolled one host back to the pre-rollout kernel and the job perf improved for that node. Will run a quick comparison across hosts. :mag:

mike_netops: Looking at NIC counters now — seeing QP retries and some QP state transitions to ERR. Could be firmware mismatch on the new nic firmware we pushed. Quick grep from dmesg:

```
rdma: mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: INF: QP 0x3a1c moved to ERR, op 0x12
mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: ERR: Completion queue entry with error 0x4
```

mike_netops: Also noticed rx packet reordering stats climbed on a subset of hosts.

luis_sre: Confirming — smoothed cluster-wide graphs show a throughput step down aligned with the OFED rollout window. Rolling back OFED on one rack fixed it within ~10m.

norman_eng: This is different from the mlx5 coalesce regression we saw earlier — those were predominantly in eu-west. This stack shows QP ERR spikes and NCCL logging: `WARN NCCL Allreduce: transport RDMA error, falling back to TCP`.

alice_research: Is anyone pinning to a specific CUDA driver ABI or NCCL version in these jobs? Could be interplay: CUDA 12.2 + driver 555.42 + ofed X.Y combo.

sam_ml: Our job specs don't pin OFED — it's infra-managed. We do pin NCCL 2.16 and CUDA 12.2 in our containers.

jenna_oncall: Action items I propose: 1) Mike, gather NIC firmware and OFED package versions for impacted hosts. 2) Luis, isolate a small test harness to reproduce allreduce between two GPUs across hosts with current stack and with rollback. 3) Norman, file a rollback playbook for affected racks and tag capacity as degraded in the scheduler.

mike_netops: On it. Current quick list: mlx5 firmware 20.30, OFED 6.1.2-rc, kernel 6.5.3, nvidia-driver 555.42. Rolling back OFED -> 6.0.9 and firmware -> 20.28 on a test node now.

deploy-bot: Deploy record: ofed-update-ap-south1 completed for rack-rm-07 at 2023-11-15T02:12:07Z by infra-ci.

luis_sre: Repro test results:
- current stack: RDMA allreduce 120 MB/s
- rollback OFED+fw: RDMA allreduce 820 MB/s (close to baseline)
So it's definitely the OFED/firmware bundle.

norman_eng: Temporary mitigation: mark ap-south-1 GPU capacity as 'reduced RDMA' in the scheduler and add automatic NCCL fallback cost adjustment so jobs choose eu-west or us-east when possible. Also notify cost team — cross-region fallback will increase egress and spot usage.

alex_infra: Agreed. I'll open an incident for rollout->regression and coordinate rollback for the next maintenance window. We need an RCA with vendor (switch vendor + NIC vendor) — pinging account rep.

sam_ml: Quick ask from ML: can we get a canary list of hosts that will keep the problematic OFED so we can re-run model evals? We need to quantify end-user model perf/regressions.

jenna_oncall: I'll keep a ring of 6 nodes with the updated stack for testing and run nightly evals. If we see functional failures besides perf, escalate to vendor support.

alice_research: Note — we should also test with NCCL env toggles: `NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX`, `NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` might mask symptoms. But root cause looks infra-side.

mike_netops: Vendor already acked receipt of logs, requested firmware/device traces. They suspect a race in mlx5 firm/fw combo.

luis_sre: Adding traceroute of kernel changes: kernel 6.5.3 changed rdma-core handshake timeouts in our config, might make QP transitions more sensitive. Will validate.

norman_eng: Long term: add pre-roll perf smoke for RDMA heavy workloads to our infra rollout pipeline and a canary ramp that forces NCCL allreduce microbenchmarks. No more fleet-wide OFED rolls without that.

alex_infra: Thanks everyone. I'll post the incident link + rollback schedule in #incidents once it's filed. For now, tag this thread with :rotating_light: and keep comms here for quick notes.

jenna_oncall: :thumbsup: keeping watch.

sam_ml: Thanks — will re-run failed experiments with eu-east fallback for now.
